title: Career Pathways of Local Madrasah Graduates
what_it_is: Career Pathways of Local Madrasah Graduates

sections.label: Madrasah pre-university student share
sections.summary: In the past three years, around 35% of students in each madrasah cohort pursue pre-university madrasah education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In the past three years, around 35% of students in each madrasah cohort, pursue pre-university madrasah education.

sections.label: Madrasah students secular pathways
sections.summary: About 70% of the rest pursue secular educational pathways, most of them about two-thirds after their O levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For the rest of the students – that means about 70% of them – they pursue a secular educational pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Most of them – about two-thirds of these 70% – do it after their "O" level.

sections.label: SUSS opportunities and Edusave parity
sections.summary: SUSS has opened lifelong learning opportunities for madrasah students, and a question is raised on parity of MUIS and MOE support, noting madrasah students are not eligible for Edusave bursaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Which is why now we also want to develop adjacent competencies and we are glad that SUSS has opened up this opportunity for madrasah students through lifelong learning opportunities; at the same time to acquire qualifications that will allow them to practise just like any other lawyer or social worker in a way that will contribute to our community, as well as in the future, if they want to go to the larger sector, they can do so too.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would just like to raise a question on the level of parity between the support given to the madrasah community by MUIS versus by MOE, in particular, as we look into the future support that is given by MOE in the sense of continuing education as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I understand that today, madrasah students are not eligible for Edusave bursaries.

sections.label: Primary madrasah Compulsory Education exemption
sections.summary: Parents who opt for their children to pursue madrasah education at the Primary school level are exempted from the Compulsory Education Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Parents who opt for their children to pursue madrasah education at the Primary school level are actually exempted from the Compulsory Education Act.

sections.label: Producing impactful religious leaders
sections.summary: The community's focus is to produce religious leaders impactful and relevant to the community and to help Singapore integrate into the multiracial, multi-religious landscape, with efforts to increase madrasah support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Having said that, for our community, our focus, as I had mentioned just now, is to produce religious leaders that will be impactful and also relevant to our community, and of course to help Singapore integrate into the multiracial, multi-religious landscape that we all are in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will try to increase the support for our madrasah with the resources that we have.

sections.label: Madrasah structure adequate but improving
sections.summary: Compared to many other places, the structure and institution of the madrasah are serving us and are adequate, but this will not be settled for and will continue to improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, if we compare ourselves to many other places, the structure and the institution of our madrasah are serving us; I would say it is adequate but I will not say that it is something we will settle for and we will continue to improve over time.
